cards.explanation: The answer is detest evil and cling to good. Romans 12:9 says, "Detest what is evil; cling to what is good." Detest is a strong word, and so is cling, friends. I know a little about clinging, because cookie dough has been stuck to my mustache since the Millers' kitchen and it is NOT letting go.
The answer is False. Romans 12:10 says, "Outdo yourselves in honoring one another." Nobody waits to be honored first. They try to beat each other to the honoring, friends.

The answer is patient. Romans 12:12 says, "Be joyful in hope, patient in affliction, persistent in prayer." Hard times are when patience is needed most, friends. Trust me, I know. Sitting in the back of a drawer for years will teach you to wait, whether you like it or not.

The answer is bless them. Romans 12:14 says, "Bless those who persecute you." I know, friends. I bet it's not the first thing anybody wants to do. But there it is in black and white, and the very next line adds, "Bless and do not curse."

The answer is to share the feeling with them. Romans 12:15 says, "Rejoice with those who rejoice; weep with those who weep." The word is WITH, bakers. When a friend is celebrating, you celebrate. When a friend is crying, you cry with them.

The answer is False. Romans 12:16 says, "Live in harmony with one another. Do not be proud, but associate with the lowly. Do not be conceited." Paul doesn't tell them to stick close to the important people. He points them toward the lowly instead, friends.

The answer is as far as it depends on them. Romans 12:18 says, "If it is possible on your part, live at peace with everyone." The verse speaks only of what's possible on their part, friends. It doesn't make peace depend on how the other person acts.

The answer is God's wrath. Romans 12:19 says, "Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God’s wrath." Paul backs it up with Scripture: "Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord." So the believers put down the scoreboard and leave the paying back to God. It's a lot less tiring that way, friends.

The answer is True. Romans 12:20 says, "If your enemy is hungry, feed him; if he is thirsty, give him a drink." Your enemy, friends, the one on the other side of the fight. Feeding him is the opposite of getting even, and it says so right there.

The answer is good, bakers! Romans 12:21 says, "Do not be overcome by evil, but overcome evil with good." Notice Paul doesn't say to answer evil with more evil. He says to overcome it with good. I think that's a mic drop of a last line.
